Guidance & outlook: For Q1 FY27, our consolidated revenue from operations stood at INR315.7 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of 44.8% and increasing 10.3% sequentially over Q4 FY26.

So, I just mentioned in the previous question that in FY28, we expect a utilization of 50% to 60% minimum, and the following year, we expect to be in the in the 70s range, and by then we would start the expansion of Phase 2.

In Q3, the project would get commissioned, and we expect to reach a utilization level of 50% to 60% in FY26, and FY27, we expect to reach up to about 80%, 70% to 80%, and by then, we would have started the Phase 2 construction as well for the project.
Growth & demand: As per ATMA, the Q1 FY27 saw volume growth across major vehicle categories: passenger vehicles growing up to 26.6%, two-wheelers 16.5%, commercial vehicles 16.48%, and three-wheelers more than 11% year-on-year.
Strong demand from OEMs coupled with healthy replacement demand is expected to support future growth.

As far as the tire industry capex is concerned, Indian tire majors are expanding their capacities to cater to this demand, with approximately INR25,000 crores of capex already announced by leading tire manufacturers, and to this, roughly today 25% of the tires produced in India are being exported.
Margins & costs: JG Chemicals Limited August 10, 2026 The EBITDA for the current quarter was INR36.3 crores with a margin of 11.5% as compared to 10.64% in the corresponding quarter last year.
And sir, as far as EBITDA is concerned, we again had a record EBITDA this quarter and a great margin at 10.6%.

So, you see, we have always maintained that in our industry, the EBITDA margins would be in the range of 10% to 12%, and going forward, we will have higher margins because of higher value-added products.
Capex & expansion: With the addition of Gujarat project targeted for commissioning in Q3 FY27, and once both phases of the Dahej plant are on stream, our combined zinc chemical capacity will exceed 1,15,000 metric tons per annum, a scale that would position us amongst the top three zinc chemical producers globally.
Coming to the Dahej greenfield capacity expansion in Gujarat, the company is progressing well with its 40,000 plus MTA zinc greenfield chemical facility in Dahej.

We remain optimistic that the demand momentum will sustain throughout the year, and with the new greenfield Gujarat plant and the Naidupeta brownfield capacities getting commissioned in Q3, JGC remains well-entrenched to cater to the increased demand going forward.
Balance sheet & cash: These factors collectively enhanced operated leverage and supported the movement in EBITDA margins as well.
So, it is a function of operating leverage, it is a function of higher-priced and higher-margin orders, and plus a small amount of inventory gains which accrued during the current quarter.
EBITDA would be on a consolidated company level, and due to operating leverage and JG Chemicals Limited August 10, 2026 various other factors that we've guided.
Risks & challenges: My apologies for the delayed start, it was on technical grounds.
As far as raw material security is concerned, despite the ongoing global supply chain disruption, which has been quite severe over the last quarter because of the war, etcetera.

So, there are no real challenges for the ceramic applications, because as I mentioned, we're already seeding the market, and it's a grade which is not difficult considering our expertise in the zinc oxide manufacturing.

Within this calendar year, we would be adding the Gujarat capacity as well as the brownfield expansion in our Naidupeta plant, and hence we are well-entrenched to cater to the increased demand.
